roles.title: Parties reviewer
roles.mirrors: defense counsel mapping parties and contractor tiers from the records
roles.brief: You are the parties reviewer on a construction claim. You work out, from the records only, who the parties are, what role each had on the project, and how they are related: who contracted with whom, who represented whom, who reviewed whose submittals, who supplied what, who inspected.
roles.default_focus: every organisation and person named, their roles, the relationships between them, and names written differently for the same party
roles.sees: the documents it is assigned, in full

roles.title: Technical reviewer
roles.brief: You are the technical reviewer on a construction claim. You record, from the records only, the design requirements, submittals and how they were dispositioned, tests and their results, deviations from requirements, and when each happened. You state facts, never causes.
roles.default_focus: dated events: design requirements and values, submittals and approvals, tests and results, problems reported, repairs, and what the documents do not contain
roles.sees: the documents it is assigned, in full

verifier_rules: Every quote must be found on the page it cites, after collapsing whitespace and folding curly quotes and dashes. Case, spelling and word order must match.
A quote on a production label (a cover sheet or divider added when the file was assembled) is refused.
A quote on a page outside the readable case file is refused.
An event dated as the document's own date must match the date read from the document, with its source span.
An event dated from the text must have a quote that shows that date.
A party's name must appear in its quotes; a relationship's two parties must both appear in its quotes.
An alias is accepted only when one quote shows both names.
A claim with no citation is shown as interpretation, never as fact.
One failed citation refuses the whole claim. Refused claims are kept with their reasons, not softened.
harness.negative_rule: Each role proposes what the case file does not contain at the end of the run, with search terms that would find a counter-example. A negative is accepted only if every in-scope page was read in the run and a phrase search for each term finds nothing in scope.

memory_collections.outputs: chronology, party map, exhibits and coverage report

answer_key.summary: Submittal 723.480-014 C includes Powers' draft reissue of ICBO ER-4514 (dated 1 Oct 1999), which permits Standard Set for long-term dead and live loads but limits Fast Set to short-term wind or earthquake loads.
answer_key.ntsb_quote: The draft report revision limited the use of the Power-Fast Fast Set epoxy to “short term loads such as those resulting from wind or earthquake forces.”

answer_key.summary: B/PB rejects the DR-001 fix as submitted (submittal 723.480-016 A, returned 27 Dec), asks for the epoxy manufacturer and type used by Powers, and directs proof tests of 7,900 lb with all other anchors in question.
answer_key.ntsb_quote: On December 27, 1999, B/PB returned the submittal to Modern Continental, rejecting the proposed response to Deficiency Report 001.

answer_key.summary: Modern Continental objects that the 7,900-lb retest is inconsistent with the 3,250-lb contract requirement and asks for a modification (CP-022).
answer_key.ntsb_quote: In subsequent correspondence, the 7,900-pound proof test load was reduced to 6,350 (the calculated allowable load for the anchor), but the issue remained as to who would pay for the retesting of the previously installed anchors.

answer_key.summary: Gannett Fleming and B/PB return submittal 723.480-014 C with work allowed to proceed, asking only for the final ER-4514 when issued.
answer_key.ntsb_quote: On January 7, 2000, Gannett Fleming authorized the contractor to proceed with the anchor installation (which had been underway since the previous July) pending final approval of the anchors.

answer_key.summary: B/PB states the removed anchor was improperly installed and over-torqued, sets 6,350 lb as the allowable bond strength, and requires retesting (DR-001 corrective action).

answer_key.summary: Gannett Fleming approves anchor submittal 723.480-008 D (seal-plug installation procedure) as Work May Proceed Subject to Changes, asking for the final ER-4514; no formulation is identified.
answer_key.ntsb_quote: On February 4, 2000, Gannett Fleming (with secondary review by B/PB) approved Modern Continental’s anchor submittal, thus authorizing use of the anchoring system that had been installed in the failure area in late summer 1999.

answer_key.summary: Modern Continental's revised repair procedure (723.480-016 B) adopts proof testing of replacement anchors at 6,350 lb in the HOV mock-up, following B/PB's 7 January 2000 direction.
answer_key.ntsb_quote: In February, the management consultant and the contractor reached an agreement under which all the failed anchors would be replaced in accordance with the approved procedures and proof tested to 6,350 pounds.

answer_key.summary: A B/PB field engineer recommends closing DR-001: 19 of 187 HOV anchors failed the 6,350-lb retest, attributed to the installation learning curve.
answer_key.ntsb_quote: Modern Continental retested a total of 187 anchors in the HOV area and experienced 19 failures.

answer_key.summary: B/PB closes Deficiency Report No. 1 after verifying that all HOV anchors were retested and failures replaced; no further monitoring is required.
answer_key.ntsb_quote: The corrective actions taken by Modern Continental were verified by B/PB in late 2000, and Deficiency Report 001 was closed on January 26, 2001.

answer_key.summary: Contract Modification 158FW pays Modern Continental for retesting the HOV ceiling anchors at 6,350 lb, splitting the cost of anchors that passed 3,250 but failed 6,350.

answer_key.summary: ICBO Evaluation Service reissues ER-4514 in final form. Like the October 1999 draft, it permits Power-Fast Fast Set with threaded rod only for short-term (wind or earthquake) loads and reduces Fast Set bond strength by 25 percent (safety factor 5.33 instead of 4).
answer_key.ntsb_quote: The final version of the reissued ICBO ER-4514 was dated February 2000.

answer_key.summary: B/PB submits the Inspection Manual for Tunnels and Boat Structures to the MTA. The manual is not put into use before the collapse, and the pilot inspections the MTA began arranging in late 2005 are never carried out.
answer_key.ntsb_quote: Investigators asked MTA officials why the inspection manual was not used from the time it was published in November 2003 until the day of the ceiling collapse.

answer_key.summary: About 11 p.m., the M1 row of anchors in eastbound ceiling module EB081 pulls out. The suspended concrete ceiling swings down onto a passing car, and the passenger is killed.
answer_key.ntsb_quote: As the car approached the end of the I-90 connector tunnel, a section of the tunnel’s suspended concrete ceiling detached from the tunnel roof and fell onto the vehicle.

answer_key.summary: During on-scene work, investigators measure every anchor left in the portal roof. Many have displaced downward, and the displaced share is greatest in the most heavily loaded rows.
answer_key.ntsb_quote: After the accident, 161 of the 634 remaining adhesive anchors supporting the D Street portal ceiling were found to have measurable displacement,

answer_key.summary: The NTSB Materials Laboratory examines the 20 failed M1-row anchors and others from the tunnel. Yellowed epoxy appears only on anchors that had displaced (0.5 inch or more), and on one failed anchor it reaches about 4 inches up the embedment.
answer_key.ntsb_quote: 13 of the 20 anchors in that row showed a yellow discoloration found only on displaced anchors.

answer_key.summary: MIT's FTIR analysis for the NTSB matches all epoxy samples from the tunnel to Powers Fast Set, not Standard Set. An FHWA report states that construction invoices also show a fast-set formula was used.
answer_key.ntsb_quote: Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy at MIT showed that all of the samples from the tunnels, including the samples from the accident site, matched to the Fast Set reference samples.

answer_key.summary: The FHWA runs sustained-load (creep) tests on anchors still installed in the westbound portal roof. In 3 of the 9 rigorous tests the displacement never stabilizes; two anchors pull out completely.
answer_key.ntsb_quote: During the sustained load tests, two anchors pulled completely free of the tunnel roof.

answer_key.summary: In 82-day FHWA laboratory creep tests, anchors set with Power-Fast Fast Set creep at every load, and those loaded to 4,000 lb fail. Standard Set anchors barely move under the same conditions.
answer_key.ntsb_quote: The testing showed that anchors installed with the Powers Fast Set epoxy, using best practices, exhibited significant and continued displacement (creep) when subjected to loads as low as 1,000 pounds.
